name: Indiana

agency.name: Indiana Department of Labor (Wage and Hour Division)

rates2026.note: Indiana Minimum Wage Law matches the federal $7.25; applies to employers of 2 or more employees not covered by the federal FLSA.

minWage.smallEmployer: The state law applies to employers of 2 or more employees (USDOL state table); most employers are covered by the federal FLSA at the same $7.25.

tipped.note: Tipped employees must receive at least $2.13/hour if the employer claims a tip credit; the employer makes up any shortfall to $7.25.

minWage.other: Training wage: $4.25/hour for employees under 20 during their first 90 consecutive calendar days with the employer.

source.quote: Indiana Minimum Wage Law $7.25 per hour ... employers must pay tipped employees at least $2.13 per hour if the employer claims a tip credit.

overtime.exemptSalaryNote: No state salary threshold above the federal $684/week.
overtime.note: State overtime rule (1.5x after 40 hours/week) covers employers not subject to the FLSA; exceptions listed in Indiana Code 22-2-2-3.

source.quote: to pay employees 1 ½ times their regular rate of pay ("Overtime compensation") when employees work more than forty (40) hours during a work week.

sickLeave.note: No Indiana law requires private employers to provide paid sick leave.

finalPay.fired: by the next regularly scheduled payday
finalPay.quit: by the next regularly scheduled payday
finalPay.ptoNote: IDOL treats accrued vacation as compensation owed pro rata at separation, unless a company policy or contract sets conditions that are not met.

source.quote: Final wages must be paid on or before the next regularly scheduled payday on which the employee would have been normally paid had the employee remained employed.

ptoSource.quote: Accrued vacation pay is considered a form of compensation. ... If there is a company policy or employment contract stipulating that certain conditions must be met ... these conditions must be met

breaks.minorsOnly: Workers under 18 scheduled for at least 6 consecutive hours must get 1 or 2 rest breaks totaling at least 30 minutes.

source.quote: In general, Indiana law does not require employers to provide adult employees lunch breaks or other breaks.

rightToWorkSource.quote: no employer, labor organization or any person may require an individual to become or remain a member of a labor organization, or pay dues, fees or assessments

notes.text: An employer that fails to pay wages on time owes the wages plus attorney fees and court costs; if the failure was not in good faith, a court orders liquidated damages of two times the wages due.

source.quote: the court shall order that the employee be paid an amount equal to two times the amount of wages due the employee as liquidated damages.

notes.text: Indiana allows a $4.25 training wage for workers under 20 during their first 90 days with an employer.

source.quote: Indiana employers may pay $4.25 per hour to employees under 20 years of age for the first 90 consecutive calendar days

uncertain: Paid sick leave: no state law exists to my knowledge, but no official page explicitly saying so was read (Indiana Code site iga.in.gov is JavaScript-only, IC 22-2-16 local-mandate preemption not read); source left null.
Final pay statute (IC 22-2-5 / 22-2-9) not read directly; value from the official IN.gov / IDOL FAQ.
The IDOL vacation FAQ says 'Yes' accrued vacation is owed but subject to policy conditions; coded as 'policy'.
